question: A man walks at 4 km/h. After 6 hours, he is overtaken by a cyclist who started 2 hours after him. What is the speed of the cyclist?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the distance covered is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time taken by **Man** = 6 hours.

Time taken by **Cyclist** = 6 − 2 = 4 hours.

Ratio of Time (**Man** : **Cyclist**) = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2.

Ratio of Speed (**Man** : **Cyclist**) = 2 : 3.

If 2 units = 4 km/h, then 3 units = 6 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **Man** = 4 km/h

Time for **Man** = 6 hours

Delay for **Cyclist** = 2 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e4fab6f2084e8895538b2ca539f1f9c8a214e5da2eadfff16df0fc57b5e25eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Distance** covered by man = 4 × 6 = 24 km

⇒ Time taken by **Cyclist** = 6 − 2 = 4 hours

⇒ Speed of **Cyclist** = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed of **Cyclist** = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Constant Distance Rule

When the distance is constant, the product of speed and time is always equal (S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂).

Average Speed

Average speed for the entire journey is calculated as Total Distance ÷ Total Time taken.</p
